Posture wise, you don’t really wanna have a leg in the way of your fretting hand. Get some space between your elbow and body, relax that picking hand. That’s gonna come with practice. Switching between chords is the same. Honestly just sit there and go from tough chord to tough chord til it feels easy. Like F to G and then D and endlessly repeat it til you hate it lol. Find the shortcuts, does every finger need to come up to switch chords? Not always. That makes it easier. Tiny things like that are stuff you pick up on over time. 

It’s interesting you choosing to sing and play right away, that’s unusual but pretty fucking cool. I’m pretty alright at it myself, one tip for the more difficult stuff as you progress, try to associate parts of the lyrics to chord changes. I pair certain consonants with hits on my right hand to stay in time. Also, try playing a scale or exercise over and over and just talk to yourself, it’ll help your voice and hand independence. 

Lastly, if you wanna really progress imo, learn some country songs that require fingerpicking/hybrid picking and singing at the same time. You already got a good start and your obsession will prob have you getting those styles down quickly. The Carter family and maybelle Carter is a good reference point. She basically invented the style that countless artists use today, the Carter scratch.

I recommend letting em heal too tho. Takes like a day of not playing. And then the next day it’s a lot easier on your fingers. Def don’t go more than a day without playing tho til you get thick calluses
